clue.text: Bit of a nag and that's the whole thing summed up, so to speak?

definitions.note: singular phrase for a plural noun naming one part of the horse

indicators.note: so to speak tells us to say the phrase out loud and keep only its sound

parts.words: that's the whole thing summed up
parts.note: four quarters added together make one whole

explanation.surface: A grumble about a nagging spouse whose complaint sums up everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a scold but is an old horse; four quarters make a whole, and said aloud that is FOREQUARTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The forequarters are the front legs, shoulders and chest of a horse, one portion of the animal.

clue.text: Waste food

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a piece of food fried in batter

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase about leftovers, but they are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter is to squander bit by bit, and a fritter is a battered, deep-fried snack such as an apple fritter.

clue.text: Twig is found in drink under middle of tree

indicators.note: middle of keeps just the central letters of the word that follows

parts.note: the two central letters of tree

indicators.note: found in places the short word inside the drink

explanation.surface: A small branch turns up in someone's pint beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' means the later piece is written below the earlier one; 'Twig' is the verb, not the small branch the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal British slang for to grasp or understand something suddenly.

clue.text: Dance in yard, about to come over unwell

parts.note: a quad is a quadrangle, an enclosed yard

indicators.note: one word coming over another covers it on both sides, wrapping round it

explanation.surface: Someone dancing in a yard is about to feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is a separate piece that wraps round the word for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A quadrille is a square dance for four couples, popular in nineteenth-century ballrooms.

clue.text: Needle nipping top from sausage

indicators.note: nipping the top off removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: a banger is British slang for a sausage

explanation.surface: A needle pinching the end off a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first letter of BANGER leaves ANGER; 'Needle' is a verb here, not the sewing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or provoke them, so it means to anger.

clue.text: Mean clothes on this evening

indicators.note: clothes is a verb here, dressing one thing in another so it sits inside

explanation.surface: A cheap outfit worn for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun but is the verb: the stingy word dresses the little word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is an adverb meaning during the present or coming evening.

clue.text: S American port covering very dry Italian dish

indicators.note: covering means the port surrounds what follows it

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port
TT means teetotal, so not drinking

explanation.surface: A rice dish served in a Brazilian port wrapped round a bone-dry wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very dry' reads as a wine description but splits into two pieces; TT (teetotal) is the convention for not drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a northern Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Token expletive in aggressive response

parts.note: a counter is a token used in games

explanation.surface: A token swear word thrown back in an angry reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterblast is a vigorous, hostile retort to an attack or argument.

clue.text: Japanese island acceptable to a certain extent, docked

indicators.note: docked means cut short, like a tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: in a way means to a certain extent

explanation.surface: A judgment that a Japanese island is only partly acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'in a way' loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is the largest of the Ryukyu Islands in southern Japan.

clue.text: Book is written on characteristic units

parts.note: genes are the units carrying inherited characteristics

explanation.surface: A book written about heredity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written on' means placed after in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Bible, telling of the Creation.

clue.text: Barrier for racehorses has jumpin' gee-gee, you might say, worried

parts.note: starting means jumping in surprise; the apostrophe drops the final g in both

indicators.note: you might say tells us to take the sound of the spoken word as letters

parts.note: ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A racehorse leaps nervously at the barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Gee-gee is British baby talk for a horse, which fits the racing picture, but here it is just two letters G.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting gate is the row of stalls that opens to begin a horse race.

clue.text: Talk about one being smarter!

indicators.note: about places the talk around the number that follows

explanation.surface: Gossip about someone who is better dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neatly fashionable, so nattier is the comparative of smart in dress.

clue.text: Boat meeting a target for renovation

indicators.note: renovation means remaking, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A boat club gathering sets itself a goal for refurbishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a sporting event of boat or yacht races.

clue.text: Disturbing the peace, louder hi-fi console by all conclusions

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so take the final letter of each word

parts.note: final letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A noisy stereo cabinet breaks the neighbourhood's quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing the peace' looks like one phrase, but only 'Disturbing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is strange and unsettling, so it is disturbing.

clue.text: Easy flitting to US, being end of the day

indicators.note: flitting means moving about, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: Moving to America made someone easy-going at the close of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights out is bedtime, when lamps go off in a dormitory or barracks at night's start.

clue.text: Approaching cups, might these be chipped?

definitions.text: Approaching cups, might these be chipped?

parts.words: Approaching cups, might these be chipped?
parts.note: surface reading: crockery near the teacups that could get damaged

parts.words: Approaching cups, might these be chipped?
parts.note: setter's reading: on a course, items near the hole are played with a short lofted shot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cups' are the holes on a green and 'chipped' is the short shot that lifts the ball towards them, not damage to china.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers chip the small dimpled spheres onto the green as they near each hole.

clue.text: Stunner or shocker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a very attractive woman
second meaning: a sudden, startling piece of news

explanation.walkthrough: Both words seem to describe one surprise, but one is a beauty and the other is news.
explanation.definitionFit: A blonde bombshell is a strikingly attractive woman, and dropping a bombshell means revealing startling news.

clue.text: Not entirely in my possession, giant island

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter short of complete, so the last goes

parts.note: the orca or killer whale is a giant of the sea

explanation.surface: A giant only partly owned by the speaker, on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorca, or Menorca, is one of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Some beer belly toned?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: six cans held together for sale

definitions.note: a description standing for the noun: a toned belly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks whether beer gives you a toned belly, a joke since it gives the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-pack is a pack of six cans of beer, and also slang for visible stomach muscles.

clue.text: Meat and gravy brought home?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: from the idiom for earning a living

explanation.walkthrough: Gravy here is slang for money; earning it is 'bringing home the bacon'. Meat and gravy suggest a roast dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, and in the idiom the earnings a breadwinner brings home.

clue.text: Person trained to serve in Italian city's territorials

parts.note: Bari is a port in southern Italy, plus the 's
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Someone trained for duty in an Italian city's reserve army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained to serve' suggests a soldier, but the service is coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A barista is a skilled server who makes espresso drinks in a coffee bar.

clue.text: Wind opening clasps over ornaments, primarily

indicators.note: something that clasps holds other things tight inside it

parts.note: a chink is a narrow opening
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A gap that holds jewellery and decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' could be a verb, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinook is a warm dry wind blowing down the eastern Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: An obligation to steal kiss, snatched without permission

indicators.note: stealing takes something and keeps it inside, so one word holds another

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone feels obliged to grab a kiss without asking.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex is to seize territory without consent, so annexed means taken without permission.

clue.text: Make money, as most experienced member

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a sketch

explanation.surface: Earning money as the senior partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make money' looks like one idea, but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the senior or most respected member of a group or profession.

clue.text: Out to lunch — as setter might be?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: crazy, in British slang
second meaning: what a setter dog may be doing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to be the crossword compiler, but it is the gun dog. Barking (mad) is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking means mad, like being out to lunch, and a setter, a breed of dog, may well bark.

clue.text: Deep and heavy, hot tray for cooking

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deep, heavy baking tray, hot and ready for the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A throaty voice or sound is low and husky, coming from deep in the throat.

clue.text: Almost everyone sent back, call for strike

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so read it right to left
almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole workforce is sent home after a call for industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a walkout, but it means to hit out.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out is to strike or attack suddenly, physically or in words.

clue.text: Big fish — try to catch majestic lot by old boat

indicators.note: catching something holds it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: have a bash means have a try
kings are a group of majesties

explanation.surface: Trying to land an enormous fish from an ancient boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply sets ARK beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The basking shark is the second-largest fish in the world, a harmless plankton feeder.
